creatures-a.why: B wins on threat readability: a hot mouth on the Long One and a Kindled that separates from the bright chamber. It gives back A's best moment, the Rimewings' cyan light landing on the floor, so the margin is small.

creatures-b.why: B fixes the two weakest creatures: the brinewyrm finally reads as a swimming wyrm and the frostbloom reads at play size. A keeps a slight edge on polyp light landing on the floor and on showing the riptide swimmer.

quarters-room.why: B adds lived-in wall conduit and better-read floor plating, which serves the hab-not-box goal; its hard round porthole spill spots are the one regression and keep the margin small.

furnishings.why: Same furnishings in both; B wins on palette coherence (slate fixtures all cool), a rug that sits on the floor and better-lit kettle, while A's floor has an artifact-like row of identical light blobs. B's lighter floor costs some dark-corner contrast, so the gap is small.

wings.why: In A the exhibit light reaches the ceiling and the room, so the wings feel lit by their showpieces. B's softer floor and stronger gem bloom are real gains, but B lets the upper third fall to near-black. Best would be A's room light combined with B's floor and bloom.
